subject: Latency & availability affecting renewal — remediation options & request
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@atlasbank.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Erik Johansen <erik.johansen@atlasbank.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Latency & availability impacting renewal — request for remediation and options

Vanessa,

We're preparing for our renewal conversation next month and wanted to raise some reliability concerns that have materially affected our production traffic over the last six weeks. In October we saw three distinct tail-latency spikes during peak batch-processing windows (10/05, 10/14, 10/27) that caused a small percentage of requests (0.9%) to exceed our 2.5s threshold and forced fallbacks to our internal cache. Those fallbacks had downstream cost and user-experience impact.

We've attached a slice of our telemetry (atlas_latency_log_oct2026.csv) highlighting the incidents and the correlated retries. This is bigger than a transient blip for us — it's put availability at the center of our renewal decision.

Before we proceed with contract renewal, we need to understand:
- What mitigation steps Redwood will commit to (short-term and technical mitigations)?
- Whether you can provide a remediation credit for the impacted windows and an SLA amendment to raise our availability target (we're currently on 99.5% uptime) to something closer to 99.9% for production-critical routes.
- If Dedicated/premium options or an availability pilot could be fast-tracked and what the timelines and costs look like.

Can we set a 30-minute call this week to review root causes and discuss commercial remedies? We'd prefer not to delay the renewal, but we need clarity on how Redwood plans to reduce tail latency and how that will be reflected contractually.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Head of Platform Reliability
Atlas Bank

Attachment: atlas_latency_log_oct2026.csv
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@atlasbank.com>
Cc: Erik Johansen <erik.johansen@atlasbank.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Latency & availability impacting renewal — request for remediation and options

Maya — thank you for the clear summary and for sending the telemetry. First, I'm sorry Atlas ran into those spikes — that falls short of the experience we aim to deliver. I reviewed the CSV quickly and want to get engineering and commercial aligned quickly.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) 30-minute technical call tomorrow (Mon 11/2) with our infra lead to walk through the telemetry and incident slices.
2) We will propose a short remediation plan and a provisional credit for the impacted windows while we investigate (we'll confirm the exact dollar/credit amount after the RCA).
3) If the issue maps to workload isolation / autoscale behavior, we can stand up a 2-week dedicated premium pilot running your critical routes — low-friction and reversible — to demonstrate improvements to tail latency.

I've attached a short plan (initial_remediation_plan.pdf) outlining the meeting agenda and what engineering will look at. I'll loop Sean from commercial and Markus from infra on this thread so we can move quickly.

I can do the call 11/2 at 10:00am PT — does that work?

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

Attachment: initial_remediation_plan.pdf
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@atlasbank.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Erik Johansen <erik.johansen@atlasbank.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Commercial options for availability — renewal amendment draft and pilot economics

Hi Maya — thanks for raising this. Appreciate the patience while we line up both technical and contractual responses. Per Vanessa's note, we recommend pairing a short technical pilot with a clear commercial amendment so Atlas has contractual recourse while we prove improvements. High-level commercial proposal: 

- Option A (Pilot + Renewal): 12-month renewal with a 15% uplift in committed Dedicated capacity for critical routes, 3 months of pro-rated service credit applied up front as a good-faith remediation for the Oct incidents.
- Option B (SLA Amendment): Add a latency/availability SLO appendix to the existing agreement that specifies target uptime 99.9% for named production routes and establishes credit tiers for outage/latency breaches.

I've uploaded a working amendment draft and a DocuSign readiness link; I'll attach the amendment file to the thread now (amendment_draft_v1.docx). If Atlas prefers the pilot path, we can fast-track a 2-week premium pilot at no incremental charge (covered by Redwood for this exchange) and then bake the results into the final amendment.

DocuSign (preview): https://www.docusign.com/recipient/view?docId=4a9e7f
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/HB-3291

If you want to accept the pilot we can start the canary within 48 hours of the call. Vanessa — please confirm the exact technical scope we will pilot so I can include the right pricing language in the amendment.

—Sean Gallagher
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

Attachment: amendment_draft_v1.docx
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@atlasbank.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 15:40:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Latency & availability impacting renewal — remediation options & request

Maya / team — quick technical note after a first-pass investigation of the logs Vanessa shared. High-level summary:
- Root cause (provisional): transient KV-cache thrash on GPU hosts during bursty batch window; autoscaler reacted but not fast enough for the observed 95th+ percentile tail. This produced higher token latencies for a small subset of requests.
- Short-term mitigations we can implement within 24–48 hours:
  * Increase aggressive pre-warm slots for the named routes during the batch window.
  * Apply KV cache pinning for your high-fanout endpoints to reduce eviction churn.
  * Lower the autoscale cooldown from 120s to 60s for your dedicated pilot lanes.
- Medium-term: dedicated lanes + workload-aware batching will dramatically reduce tail latency — that's what the 2-week pilot will prove.

I'll attach a one-page root cause summary and a suggested tuning patch we can apply as part of the pilot (root_cause_summary.txt). Operationally we can run the pilot in your us-west region with explicit rollback flags so we can revert the changes if you see any regression.

Markus Klein
Lead, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai

Attachment: root_cause_summary.txt
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@atlasbank.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Latency & availability impacting renewal — remediation options & request

Thanks all — the plan and the proposed pilot sound reasonable. We're prepared to proceed on the pilot under the following conditions before we start:

1) We require a written amendment that documents the pilot scope, the rollback procedure, and an interim availability target for the piloted routes (we'd like to see 99.9% target for the named production lanes).
2) We need an immediate remediation credit applied to the next invoice for the confirmed impacted windows; please propose a concrete dollar credit and the calculation methodology.
3) Procurement will need a 48-hour review of any signed DocuSign amendment (I attach our procurement guidance document for the internal procurement checklist).

If you can get an updated amendment (showing the pilot scope and explicit SLO language) and a proposed credit calculation by EOD Mon 11/8, we'll schedule the pilot start for Wed 11/10. Otherwise we'll need to push the renewal conversation.

Best,
Maya
Head of Platform Reliability | Atlas Bank
maya.patel@atlasbank.com

Attachment: procurement_guidance.docx
